title: Shell vs Environment Variables and PATH: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on shell variables versus environment variables, export, PATH lookup, startup files, env/printenv, per-command variables and how sudo treats the environment.

chapters.title: Shell vs Environment Variables: The Mental Model
points: Shell variable: exists only inside the current shell process, set with NAME=value (no spaces around =), read with $NAME
Environment variable: a shell variable marked for export; copied into the environment of every child process the shell starts
Inheritance is one-way and by copy: a child gets a snapshot at fork/exec, and its changes never flow back to the parent
Example: FOO=1; bash -c 'echo $FOO' prints nothing, but export FOO; bash -c 'echo $FOO' prints 1
Mistake: 'FOO = 1' with spaces runs a command named FOO with args '=' and '1' (command not found)

chapters.title: export and Setting Variables for One Command
points: export NAME=value sets and exports in one step; export NAME exports an existing shell variable; export -n NAME removes the export flag
Exported changes affect only children started afterwards; already-running processes keep their old copy
One-shot prefix: NAME=value cmd puts NAME in cmd's environment only, and the shell's own variable is unchanged
Prefix form vs export: prefix lasts for one command, export lasts for the rest of the session and all its children
Mistake: FOO=1 echo $FOO prints empty, because $FOO is expanded by the shell before the prefix takes effect; use FOO=1 sh -c 'echo $FOO'
unset NAME removes the variable entirely; NAME= only sets it to empty (still defined)

chapters.title: PATH Lookup, which and type
points: PATH is a colon-separated list of directories; the shell searches them left to right and runs the first executable match
Lookup order for a command name: alias, function, builtin, then PATH search (name containing / skips PATH)
type cmd shows how the shell would resolve it (alias, builtin, function, or file); type -a lists all matches in order
which cmd only searches PATH (an external program), so it misses aliases and builtins; prefer type or command -v in scripts
Append safely: export PATH="$PATH:/new/dir" (end = lowest priority); prepend with PATH="/new/dir:$PATH" to override system tools
hash -r clears the shell's cached command locations after installing or moving a binary
Mistakes: export PATH=/new/dir (overwrites PATH, breaks ls); a trailing or empty entry in PATH means the current directory; running a local script needs ./script

chapters.title: Startup Files: ~/.bashrc vs ~/.profile
points: Login shell (SSH, console login, bash -l) reads /etc/profile, then the first of ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, ~/.profile
Interactive non-login shell (new terminal tab, running bash) reads ~/.bashrc only
Scripts run non-interactively read neither by default; they inherit the parent's environment
Convention: put exported variables and PATH in ~/.profile (once per login); put aliases, prompt and functions in ~/.bashrc (every interactive shell)
Fix for the split: have ~/.bash_profile or ~/.profile source ~/.bashrc, so login shells also get aliases
Edits do not apply to the open shell: run source ~/.bashrc (or . ~/.bashrc) or open a new shell; ~/.profile changes need re-login
Mistake: appending to PATH in ~/.bashrc without a guard grows PATH on every nested shell or re-source

chapters.title: env, printenv and sudo with the Environment
points: printenv lists exported variables; printenv NAME prints one value (no $ and exit status 1 if unset); env with no args prints the same list
env NAME=value cmd runs cmd with an extra variable; env -i cmd runs it with an empty environment; env -u NAME removes one
set (no args) lists shell variables and functions too, so it shows more than env/printenv
sudo resets the environment by default (env_reset): most of your variables are dropped and PATH becomes secure_path from sudoers
Pass variables explicitly: sudo VAR=value cmd, or sudo -E to preserve the environment (still limited by sudoers policy); sudo env PATH="$PATH" cmd to carry your PATH
Mistake: a tool found in your PATH gives 'command not found' under sudo because secure_path ignores your PATH; use the full path
Mistake: sudo echo $HOME expands $HOME in your shell before sudo runs; use sudo sh -c 'echo $HOME' to expand it inside

chapters.title: Cheat Sheet: Variables, PATH and Startup Files
points: Set: VAR=v (shell only) | export VAR=v (inherited by children) | VAR=v cmd (one command) | unset VAR
Inspect: printenv VAR | env | set | echo "$VAR"
PATH: export PATH="$PATH:/dir" (append), PATH="/dir:$PATH" (prepend), echo "$PATH" | tr : '\n'
Resolve: type -a cmd | command -v cmd | which cmd | hash -r
Startup: login -> /etc/profile + ~/.profile; interactive non-login -> ~/.bashrc; reload with source ~/.bashrc
sudo: env reset + secure_path; use sudo VAR=v cmd, sudo -E, or full paths; sudo sh -c '...' for in-root expansion
